claims.text: A refined lamellar microstructure combined with Y and Hf additions promotes rapid, selective oxidation of Al.
Selective oxidation of Al produces a continuous, protective Al2O3 scale.
The continuous Al2O3 scale enhances long-term oxidation resistance and material integrity under harsh high-temperature conditions.
Controlled cooling can produce a refined lamellar microstructure in the NiCoCrAl-based alloy.
The underlying lamellar or dendritic microstructure governs the morphology, continuity, and uniformity of the resulting Al2O3 scale.
A refined lamellar structure enhances preferential and rapid oxidation of Al relative to a conventional dendritic structure.
The refined lamellar structure promotes formation of a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale.
Y and Hf stabilize the oxide scale by modifying interfacial energies and diffusion kinetics.
Scale stabilization by Y and Hf reduces oxide spallation and improves long-term oxidation resistance.
The lamellar alloy will have approximately 50–60% lower thermally grown oxide growth rates than the dendritic control.
The lamellar alloy will experience fewer oxide-scale spallation events than the dendritic control.
The proposed microstructure-dependent oxidation mechanism should operate from 800 °C to 1200 °C in oxidative conditions.
Outside 800–1200 °C or under different atmospheres, the behavior governing oxidation resistance may differ.
